title: Multimodal Foundation Models for Industrial Dataset Generation: Methods, Evidence, and Open Challenges
abstract: Industrial dataset generation (IDG) must preserve task-relevant defects, operating conditions, cross-modal relationships, and provenance. This critical review examines how pretrained multimodal foundation models (MFMs) and their components contribute to reusable manufacturing datasets through direct synthesis, assisted annotation, and tool-mediated construction. We compare visual inspection, numerical time series, engineering geometry, and process-linked observations by model role, conditioning resources, output interface, and validation setting, retaining conventional generators as explicit comparators. Three findings organize the synthesis. First, supervision and inference resources determine the meaning of few-shot, zero-shot, and training-free claims; frozen weights can coexist with inference-time embedding optimization. Second, the generated artifact determines the checks: image labels require boundary verification, numerical outputs require units and acquisition context, and CAD programs require execution and geometry assessment. Third, reported gains are conditional on each study's data access, split, metric, and resource budget. A six-stage lifecycle connects these comparisons to source acquisition, alignment, adaptation, screening, independent validation, and release. The resulting evaluation guidance separates artifact quality from real-task utility and supports traceable reporting of constraints, uncertainty, and cost. The mapped evidence is strongest for visual defect synthesis and CAD construction; calibrated multichannel generation and longitudinal production validation remain less established.
